title: Context Language Models: Self-Managing Context to Improve Performance and Reduce Compute Costs
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/context-language-models/en/headerimage/gemini-agentic-vision-1791724239724.jpg"/><p>Researchers from Meta, MIT, and the University of Washington introduce Context Language Models (CLMs), a new approach that enables language models to manage and edit their own context rather than relying on predefined mechanisms for summarization, compression, and information retrieval, reporting substantial gains in both performance and computational efficiency.</p> <i>By Sergio De Simone</i>

title: Foresight AI Brings Gremlin Agents to Reliability Engineering
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/gremlin-foresight-ai/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1791653267864.jpg"/><p>Reliability management company Gremlin has announced the general availability of Foresight AI, an agentic product that analyses services for potential failures, recommends changes and reruns tests to check that a fix works.</p> <i>By Matt Saunders</i>

title: AWS Introduces Enhanced Custom Event Buses for EventBridge
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/aws-enhanced-eventbridge-buses/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1790663976977.jpg"/><p>AWS recently announced enhanced custom event buses for Amazon EventBridge, allowing organizations to share a centralized bus across accounts with ordered delivery, simplified subscriber management, event replay, content-based deduplication, and a new publisher/subscriber-based pricing model.</p> <i>By Renato Losio</i>

title: Cloudflare Traces Turns the Proxy Layer into OpenTelemetry Spans, with New Volume-Based Pricing
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/cloudflare-traces-open-beta/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1791443919168.jpg"/><p>Cloudflare has put Traces into open beta, extending automatic tracing from Workers to security rules, transformations, cache, routing and origin handling as OpenTelemetry spans. Traces accept and forward W3C traceparent headers, and Trace Rules allow targeted sampling. Pricing moves to ingestion and retention volume from December 1.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

title: Android Bench 2 Adds Support for Long-Horizon Tasks, Agentic Evaluation, and Continuous Scoring
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/android-bench-2/en/headerimage/cloudflare-computer-agents-1791561634896.jpeg"/><p>Google has released Android Bench 2.0, a major update to its benchmark framework for evaluating AI models and agents on Android development tasks. The update introduces long-horizon tasks (LHTs), agent-based evaluation, and continuous scoring to better assess performance on complex, multi-step development tasks.</p> <i>By Sergio De Simone</i>

title: Shopify Upgrades Checkout Blocks to Polaris Web Components, Cutting Bundle Sizes up to 85%
partialText: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>Shopify has updated its Checkout Blocks app, transitioning five high-traffic checkout UI extensions to remote-dom using Preact and Polaris web components. The rewrite, which involved moving to TypeScript and a new API version, led to significant reductions in bundle sizes and load times. From October 1, 2026, only the updated versions will be supported.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

title: Github Migrates Copilot Runtime to Rust with AI-Assisted Rewrite
partialText: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>GitHub migrated more than 800,000 lines of Copilot runtime code from TypeScript and Node.js to Rust in about 14.5 weeks using AI-assisted development. The incremental migration used N-API interoperability, automated testing, human review, and 128 pull requests while continuing to ship releases.</p> <i>By Leela Kumili</i>

title: CircleCI Makes Machine Runner Orchestrator Generally Available
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/circleci-machine-runner/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1790836191409.jpg"/><p>CircleCI has made its Machine Runner Orchestrator 1.0.0 generally available, providing automated scaling of self-hosted machine runner virtual machines according to CI workload demand.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>

title: Presentation: Ontology‐Driven Observability: Building the E2E Knowledge Graph at Netflix Scale
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/netflix-observability-aiops-ontology-scale/en/mediumimage/medium-1790845339712.jpg"/><p>Prasanna Vijayanathan and Renzo Sanchez-Silva share how Netflix tackles observability across 38M events/sec. They discuss replacing reactive monitoring with an AI-driven operational ontology and agentic workflows using Claude and graph databases. They explain how unifying MELT telemetry into queryable knowledge graphs enables automated triaging, root-cause analysis, and self-healing systems.</p> <i>By Prasanna Vijayanathan, Renzo Sanchez-Silva</i>

title: Olson and Söderqvist Discuss Valkey’s Evolution and Future Past Caching Use Cases at OSS EU
partialText: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>Valkey is a growing project, launched as a fork of Redis over two years ago, supported by twelve maintainers and nine committee members from various companies. Recent developments include enhanced throughput, improved cluster functionality, and plans for features like synchronous replication and tiered storage. The project also emphasises security and release efficiency through automation.</p> <i>By Olimpiu Pop</i>

title: Podcast: The Minimum Viable Manager: Building Trust, Feedback, and Alignment
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/podcasts/building-trust-feedback-alignment/en/smallimage/engineering-culture-500-1790863262988.jpg"/><p>In this podcast, Shane Hastie, Lead Editor for Culture & Methods, spoke to Matt Gjertsen, founder of Built and author of Minimum Viable Manager, about the three foundational skills every first-time manager needs, how to build trust and give effective feedback, and why human leadership skills matter even more in the age of AI.</p> <i>By Matt Gjertsen</i>

title: HashiCorp Relased Terraform Google Cloud Provider 8.0 in General Availability
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/terraform-google-cloud-provider/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1791470649216.jpg"/><p>HashiCorp has announced the general availability of version 8.0 of the Terraform provider for Google Cloud. The major release updates the default load balancing for two Compute Engine resources. It also removes resources linked to retired Google Cloud services.</p> <i>By Claudio Masolo</i>

title: Cloudflare K2 Builds Event Streams on R2 Object Storage, at a Second of Produce Latency
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/cloudflare-k2-serverless-streams/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1791040228747.jpg"/><p>Cloudflare has launched K2 in public beta, a serverless event streaming service implementing a durable log on R2 object storage. Cloudflare states produce latency of about one second at p99; a tester reported end-to-end p99 of 7.5 seconds, which a commenter answering for the team said was higher than expected. Consume charges match produce charges per GB.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

title: Presentation: Multi-Agent Patterns from Spotify’s AI Powered Advertising Platform
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/spotify-multi-agent-ai-architecture/en/mediumimage/pratik-rasam-medium-1790847111671.jpeg"/><p>Pratik Rasam discusses how Spotify Ads Manager runs production-grade multi-agent systems at scale using Google ADK Java. He shares key architectural patterns, domain ownership models, deterministic guardrails, and tracing-based evaluation strategies, detailing hard-learned lessons on drawing agent boundaries, optimizing tool schemas, and managing costs while avoiding monolithic agent pitfalls.</p> <i>By Pratik Rasam</i>

title: Technological Sovereignty Requires Choice, Skills, and Support, Panelists Say During OSS EU
partialText: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>European organisations can enhance their technological sovereignty by developing credible alternatives and acquiring necessary skills, rather than completely avoiding global providers. A panel discussion at the OSS EU highlighted the importance of understanding dependencies in cloud and hardware, and emphasized the need for practical choices in software for effective operational sovereignty.</p> <i>By Olimpiu Pop</i>
